records.source: וַֽיִּקְרְב֞וּ רָאשֵׁ֣י הָֽאָב֗וֹת לְמִשְׁפַּ֤חַת בְּנֵֽי־גִלְעָד֙ בֶּן־מָכִ֣יר בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה מִֽמִּשְׁפְּחֹ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י יוֹסֵ֑ף וַֽיְדַבְּר֞וּ לִפְנֵ֤י מֹשֶׁה֙ וְלִפְנֵ֣י הַנְּשִׂאִ֔ים רָאשֵׁ֥י אָב֖וֹת לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And drew near [the] heads of the fathers of [the] clan of [the] sons of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh, of [the] clans of [the] sons of Joseph, and spoke before Moses and before the leaders, heads of fathers of [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: Then the heads of the families in the clan of Gilead's descendants came forward. Gilead was the son of Machir, son of Manasseh, and belonged to the clans of Joseph's descendants. They spoke before Moses and the leaders, the heads of the ancestral families of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.1: And the heads of the fathers of the clan of the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh, of the clans of the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of Joseph, drew near and spoke before Moses and before the leaders, the heads of the fathers of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.1: Then the family leaders from the clan of Gilead came forward. Gilead was the son of Machir and the grandson of Manasseh, from the family line of Joseph. They spoke to Moses and to the leaders who headed the families of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: the clan of Gilead: the clan of Zelophehad, whose daughters' case was settled in chapter 27
decisions.reason: Zelophehad son of Hepher belonged to the clan of Gilead (26:29-33; 27:1). The LORD had ruled that his daughters should receive his share of the land (27:1-11). Now the leaders of his clan come back to that ruling, because it leaves a question open: what happens to the land when the daughters marry.

decisions.choice: heads of the fathers: the heads of the ancestral families
decisions.reason: The phrase is a short form of "heads of the house of the fathers" (1:4; 7:2), the men who led the extended families within each clan. The same title is used for the leaders of all Israel at the end of the verse.

decisions.choice: Gilead son of Machir: a clan of Manasseh, one of the two tribes descended from Joseph
decisions.reason: Machir was Manasseh's son and Gilead was Machir's son (26:29). Joseph's sons Ephraim and Manasseh each became a tribe (Genesis 48:5), so "the clans of the sons of Joseph" here means the clans of Manasseh.

decisions.choice: descendants / sons
decisions.reason: The "sons" of Gilead and of Joseph are the people of those clans, men and women. Literal gives "descendants" with "sons" as the traditional form; Balanced says "descendants" and Readable names the clan and family line.

records.heading: The inheritance of daughters who marry

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ אֶת־אֲדֹנִי֙ צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה לָתֵ֨ת אֶת־הָאָ֧רֶץ בְּנַחֲלָ֛ה בְּגוֹרָ֖ל לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽאדֹנִי֙ צֻוָּ֣ה בַֽיהוָ֔ה לָתֵ֗ת אֶֽת־נַחֲלַ֛ת צְלָפְחָ֥ד אָחִ֖ינוּ לִבְנֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And they said, my lord commanded Yahweh to give the land as inheritance by lot to [the] sons of Israel, and my lord was commanded by Yahweh to give [the] inheritance of Zelophehad our brother to his daughters.
pieces: They said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} commanded you, my lord, to give the land to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} as an inheritance by lot, and you, my lord, were commanded by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

L.2: And they said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} commanded my lord to give the land as an inheritance by lot to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and my lord was commanded by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother to his daughters.

R.2: They said, "Sir, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded you to give the land to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} by lot, so that each family would receive its share. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} also commanded you to give the land of our relative Zelophehad to his daughters.

decisions.choice: my lord: a respectful way of addressing Moses
decisions.reason: Speaking to someone of higher rank, a person could call him "my lord" instead of "you" (Genesis 44:18; Numbers 11:28; 32:25). The leaders are speaking to Moses himself.

decisions.choice: by lot: the land shared out by lot among the tribes
decisions.reason: The LORD had told Moses that the land would be divided by lot, with larger tribes receiving larger shares (26:52-56; 33:54). Each family's share was its inheritance, to be kept in the family.

decisions.choice: the inheritance of Zelophehad to his daughters: the ruling of 27:1-11
decisions.reason: The leaders do not dispute that ruling. They quote both commands side by side, the sharing of land by tribe and the gift to the daughters, because together they raise the problem set out in verses 3-4.

decisions.choice: our brother: our kinsman
decisions.reason: Zelophehad was a member of their clan, not their brother by birth. The word "brother" is often used for a relative or fellow member of a clan or tribe (Genesis 13:8; Leviticus 25:25).

decisions.choice: you, my lord / Sir ... you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of Moses as "my lord" in the third person. Balanced adds "you" beside the title so it is clear Moses is the one addressed; Readable uses "Sir" and "you".

decisions.choice: so that each family would receive its share
decisions.reason: Readable explains what giving the land "as an inheritance" means, since the rest of the chapter turns on each family's share.

records.source: וְ֠הָיוּ לְאֶחָ֞ד מִבְּנֵ֨י שִׁבְטֵ֥י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ לְנָשִׁים֒ וְנִגְרְעָ֤ה נַחֲלָתָן֙ מִנַּחֲלַ֣ת אֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ וְנוֹסַ֕ף עַ֚ל נַחֲלַ֣ת הַמַּטֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּהְיֶ֖ינָה לָהֶ֑ם וּמִגֹּרַ֥ל נַחֲלָתֵ֖נוּ יִגָּרֵֽעַ׃
records.gloss: And [if] they become to one of [the] sons of [the] tribes of [the] sons of Israel as wives, then will be withdrawn their inheritance from [the] inheritance of our fathers, and will be added to [the] inheritance of the tribe which they will belong to them; and from [the] lot of our inheritance it will be withdrawn.
pieces: But if they become the wives of men from one of the other tribes of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of our ancestors and added to the inheritance of the tribe they will then belong to. So it will be taken away from the share that fell to us by lot.

L.3: And [if] they become wives to one of the sons of the tribes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, then their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of our fathers and will be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they will belong; and it will be taken away from the lot of our inheritance.

R.3: What if they marry men from other tribes of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}? Then their land will be taken away from our family's land and become part of the land of the other tribe. So the land we received by lot will become smaller.

decisions.choice: become wives to one of the sons of the tribes: marry men of another tribe
decisions.reason: A married woman's land would pass to her husband and their children, who belonged to his tribe. If the daughters married outside Manasseh, their father's share would end up in another tribe's territory. The words "the tribe to which they will belong" make plain that another tribe is meant.

decisions.choice: taken away: subtracted, so that the whole is made smaller
decisions.reason: The verb means to take away from something or reduce it. It is the word the daughters used when they asked why their father's name should be "taken away" from his clan (27:4); now the clan fears its land will be taken away from in the same way.

decisions.choice: the lot of our inheritance: the share that fell to the tribe by lot
decisions.reason: The "lot" here stands for the portion received by lot (26:55-56). The leaders fear that the share the LORD assigned to their tribe will shrink.

decisions.choice: men from one of the other tribes / other tribes
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "men" and "another" or "other", which the Hebrew leaves to the context: the rest of the verse speaks of the land passing to a different tribe.

records.source: וְאִם־יִהְיֶ֣ה הַיֹּבֵל֮ לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וְנֽוֹסְפָה֙ נַחֲלָתָ֔ן עַ֚ל נַחֲלַ֣ת הַמַּטֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּהְיֶ֖ינָה לָהֶ֑ם וּמִֽנַּחֲלַת֙ מַטֵּ֣ה אֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ יִגָּרַ֖ע נַחֲלָתָֽן׃
records.gloss: And if will be the jubilee of [the] sons of Israel, then will be added their inheritance to [the] inheritance of the tribe which they will belong to them, and from [the] inheritance of [the] tribe of our fathers will be withdrawn their inheritance.
pieces: And when the Jubilee of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} arrives, their inheritance will be joined to the inheritance of the tribe they then belong to, and the inheritance of our ancestral tribe will lose it."

L.4: And when the Jubilee of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel comes, then their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they will belong, and their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of the tribe of our fathers."

R.4: Even in the Year of Jubilee, when land goes back to the families it came from, their land will not come back to us. It will stay with the tribe they married into, and our tribe will lose it for good."

decisions.choice: the Jubilee: the fiftieth year, when land that had been sold went back to its family
decisions.reason: In the Jubilee every family returned to its own land (Leviticus 25:10-13, 28). But land that passed by marriage and inheritance had not been sold, so the Jubilee would not bring it back. Instead, the Jubilee would confirm it as the other tribe's lasting property. The leaders' point is that not even the Jubilee could undo the loss.

decisions.choice: if: here "when"
decisions.reason: The word usually means "if", but the Jubilee was sure to come, so the clause states the time when the loss would be made final.

decisions.choice: Even ... when land goes back to the families it came from, their land will not come back to us ... for good
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the Jubilee was and why the leaders mention it, which the Hebrew leaves to the reader who knows Leviticus 25. Literal and Balanced keep the plain statement.

records.source: וַיְצַ֤ו מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַל־פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר כֵּ֛ן מַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי־יוֹסֵ֖ף דֹּבְרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And commanded Moses [the] sons of Israel by [the] mouth of Yahweh, saying: Right [the] tribe of [the] sons of Joseph [are] speaking.
pieces: Then Moses gave the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} this command at the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: "The tribe of Joseph's descendants is right in what it says.

L.5: And Moses commanded the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel by the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "The tribe of the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of Joseph is speaking right.

R.5: So Moses gave the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} a command from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He said, "The tribe of Joseph's descendants is right.

decisions.choice: by the mouth of the LORD: at the LORD's command
decisions.reason: Moses does not decide the case himself. As with the daughters' own request (27:5), the ruling comes from the LORD, and Moses passes it on to the people.

decisions.choice: right: their claim is just
decisions.reason: The same verdict was given on the daughters' claim (27:7). Both claims are upheld: the daughters keep their father's land, and the tribe keeps its share of the land.

decisions.choice: the tribe of the sons of Joseph: here the tribe of Manasseh
decisions.reason: The speakers are of Manasseh (verse 1), one of the two tribes descended from Joseph.

decisions.choice: is right in what it says
decisions.reason: As in 27:7, Balanced and Readable turn "speaking right" into a plain statement that their claim is right.

records.source: זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה לִבְנ֤וֹת צְלָפְחָד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לַטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם תִּהְיֶ֣ינָה לְנָשִׁ֑ים אַ֗ךְ לְמִשְׁפַּ֛חַת מַטֵּ֥ה אֲבִיהֶ֖ם תִּהְיֶ֥ינָה לְנָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: This [is] the word which commanded Yahweh concerning [the] daughters of Zelophehad, saying: to the good in their eyes they shall become wives; only to [the] clan of [the] tribe of their father they shall become wives.
pieces: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commands for the daughters of Zelophehad: 'They are free to marry the man they prefer, as long as he is from a clan of their father's tribe.

L.6: This [is] the word which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, 'To whoever is good in their eyes let them become wives; only into the clan of the tribe of their father shall they become wives.

R.6: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commands about the daughters of Zelophehad: 'They may marry anyone they choose. But the man must belong to a clan of their father's tribe.

decisions.choice: to the good in their eyes: whomever they think best
decisions.reason: To be "good in someone's eyes" means to seem right or pleasing to them. The daughters choose their own husbands; the only limit is the tribe.

decisions.choice: their eyes, their father: the pronouns are masculine but refer to the daughters
decisions.reason: As in 27:7, the pronouns have masculine forms though the daughters are meant. Hebrew sometimes uses masculine forms for a group of women; the meaning is not affected.

decisions.choice: the clan of the tribe of their father: a family within their father's tribe
decisions.reason: The phrase names the clan as part of the tribe. The reason given in verses 7-9 is that land must not pass from tribe to tribe, so the limit that matters is the father's tribe.

decisions.choice: the man they prefer, as long as he is from / the man must belong to
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable speak of "the man" to make clear that the limit is on the husband, where the Hebrew says only "to the clan".

records.source: וְלֹֽא־תִסֹּ֤ב נַחֲלָה֙ לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִמַּטֶּ֖ה אֶל־מַטֶּ֑ה כִּ֣י אִ֗ישׁ בְּנַחֲלַת֙ מַטֵּ֣ה אֲבֹתָ֔יו יִדְבְּק֖וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And not shall go around an inheritance of [the] sons of Israel from tribe to tribe; for each to [the] inheritance of [the] tribe of his fathers shall cling [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: An inheritance of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} must not change hands from tribe to tribe, for each of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} is to hold fast to the inheritance of their ancestral tribe.

L.7: And an inheritance of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel shall not go around from tribe to tribe, for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel shall cling, {{gender:each one|each man}}, to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.

R.7: The land of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} must not move from one tribe to another. Every one of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} must keep the land of the tribe their family comes from.

decisions.choice: go around: pass over, change hands
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn or go around. Of property it means to pass from one holder to another, here from one tribe to another.

decisions.choice: cling: hold fast, keep firmly
decisions.reason: The verb means to stick or hold fast to something, as a man holds fast to his wife (Genesis 2:24). Each Israelite is to keep the land of his own tribe and not let it go.

decisions.choice: the inheritance of the tribe: land given by the LORD to each tribe for good
decisions.reason: The land belonged to the LORD, who gave each tribe and family its share (Leviticus 25:23). The law keeps the shares as the LORD assigned them by lot.

decisions.choice: land
decisions.reason: As in 27:9, Readable says "land" for the inheritance, since the inheritance meant here is a share of the land.

records.source: וְכָל־בַּ֞ת יֹרֶ֣שֶׁת נַחֲלָ֗ה מִמַּטּוֹת֮ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ לְאֶחָ֗ד מִמִּשְׁפַּ֛חַת מַטֵּ֥ה אָבִ֖יהָ תִּהְיֶ֣ה לְאִשָּׁ֑ה לְמַ֗עַן יִֽירְשׁוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִ֖ישׁ נַחֲלַ֥ת אֲבֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And every daughter possessing an inheritance from [the] tribes of [the] sons of Israel, to one of [the] clan of [the] tribe of her father she shall become a wife, so that may possess [the] sons of Israel each [the] inheritance of his fathers.
pieces: Any daughter who comes into an inheritance in one of the tribes of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} is to become the wife of a man from a clan of her father's tribe. In this way each of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} will keep possession of their ancestors' inheritance.

L.8: And every daughter who possesses an inheritance from the tribes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel shall become a wife to one of the clan of the tribe of her father, so that the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel may possess, {{gender:each one|each man}}, the inheritance of his fathers.

R.8: A daughter who is given her family's land must marry a man whose clan is part of her father's tribe. That way each of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} will keep the land of their ancestors.

decisions.choice: every daughter: a law for every heiress, not only for this family
decisions.reason: As the daughters' case became a law for all Israel (27:8), so does this one. Any woman who inherits land because there is no son is to marry within her father's tribe.

decisions.choice: possesses / may possess: holds land by inheritance
decisions.reason: The verb means to take or hold possession, often of land received by inheritance. The daughter holds the land, and the aim is that every family of Israel goes on holding its own.

decisions.choice: a man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "a man" where the Hebrew says "one" of the clan; the one meant is her husband.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־תִסֹּ֧ב נַחֲלָ֛ה מִמַּטֶּ֖ה לְמַטֶּ֣ה אַחֵ֑ר כִּי־אִישׁ֙ בְּנַ֣חֲלָת֔וֹ יִדְבְּק֕וּ מַטּ֖וֹת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And not shall go around an inheritance from tribe to tribe another; for each to its inheritance shall cling [the] tribes of [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: An inheritance must not change hands from one tribe to another, for each tribe of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} is to hold fast to its own inheritance.'"

L.9: And an inheritance shall not go around from a tribe to another tribe, for the tribes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel shall cling, each one, to its own inheritance.'"

R.9: Land must not move from one tribe to another. Each tribe of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} must keep its own land.'"

decisions.choice: the rule of verse 7 repeated, now for the tribes
decisions.reason: Verse 7 says each Israelite is to hold on to the land of his tribe; this verse says the same of the tribes themselves. The repetition closes the ruling and makes it firm.

decisions.choice: each: each tribe
decisions.reason: The word is "man", used here as "each" for every one of the tribes, not for a person.

decisions.choice: closing quotation marks
decisions.reason: The LORD's word, quoted by Moses from verse 6, and Moses' speech from verse 5 both end here.

records.source: כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֑ה כֵּ֥ן עָשׂ֖וּ בְּנ֥וֹת צְלָפְחָֽד׃
records.gloss: Just as commanded Yahweh Moses, so did [the] daughters of Zelophehad.
pieces: The daughters of Zelophehad did just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

L.10: Just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses, so the daughters of Zelophehad did.

R.10: The daughters of Zelophehad did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

decisions.choice: just as ... so did: they obeyed in full
decisions.reason: This is the formula Numbers uses for obedience to a command given through Moses (1:54; 2:34). The next two verses say how the daughters carried it out.

records.source: וַתִּהְיֶ֜ינָה מַחְלָ֣ה תִרְצָ֗ה וְחָגְלָ֧ה וּמִלְכָּ֛ה וְנֹעָ֖ה בְּנ֣וֹת צְלָפְחָ֑ד לִבְנֵ֥י דֹדֵיהֶ֖ן לְנָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And became Mahlah, Tirzah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Noah, [the] daughters of Zelophehad, to [the] sons of their uncles as wives.
pieces: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, married the sons of their uncles.

L.11: And Mahlah, Tirzah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, became wives to the sons of their uncles.

R.11: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah and Noah were Zelophehad's daughters. They all married their cousins, the sons of their father's brothers.

decisions.choice: the names in a different order from 26:33 and 27:1
decisions.reason: There the order is Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah; here Tirzah comes second and Noah last. The text gives no reason for the change, and it does not affect the meaning.

decisions.choice: the sons of their uncles: their cousins on their father's side
decisions.reason: The word for "uncle" usually means a father's brother (Leviticus 10:4; 25:49). Marrying their cousins kept the land within their father's own clan, closer than the law required.

decisions.choice: their cousins, the sons of their father's brothers
decisions.reason: Readable names the relationship and explains it; Literal and Balanced keep "the sons of their uncles".

records.source: מִֽמִּשְׁפְּחֹ֛ת בְּנֵֽי־מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה בֶן־יוֹסֵ֖ף הָי֣וּ לְנָשִׁ֑ים וַתְּהִי֙ נַחֲלָתָ֔ן עַל־מַטֵּ֖ה מִשְׁפַּ֥חַת אֲבִיהֶֽן׃
records.gloss: From [the] clans of [the] sons of Manasseh son of Joseph they became wives, and was their inheritance with [the] tribe of [the] clan of their father.
pieces: It was into clans descended from Manasseh son of Joseph that they married, so their inheritance stayed with the tribe of their father's clan.

L.12: To [men] from the clans of the {{gender:descendants|sons}} of Manasseh son of Joseph they became wives, and their inheritance was with the tribe of the clan of their father.

R.12: They married men from the clans of Manasseh, Joseph's son. So their land stayed in the tribe their father's clan belonged to.

decisions.choice: their inheritance stayed: both rulings were kept
decisions.reason: The daughters kept their father's share, and the tribe kept its land. Joshua 17:3-6 tells how they later received their land among the clans of Manasseh, as the LORD had commanded.

decisions.choice: was with the tribe: remained in the tribe
decisions.reason: The verb "was" with "with" here means that the land went on belonging to the tribe; it did not pass elsewhere.

decisions.choice: to [men] from / married into / married men from
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says they "became wives from the clans", meaning wives of men from those clans. Literal brackets "men"; Balanced and Readable say "married".

records.source: אֵ֣לֶּה הַמִּצְוֺ֞ת וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בְּעַֽרְבֹ֣ת מוֹאָ֔ב עַ֖ל יַרְדֵּ֥ן יְרֵחֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: These [are] the commandments and the judgments which commanded Yahweh by [the] hand of Moses to [the] sons of Israel in [the] plains of Moab by [the] Jordan [of] Jericho.
pieces: These are the commandments and rulings that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} through Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.

L.13: These [are] the commandments and the judgments which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded by the hand of Moses to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan [across from] Jericho.

R.13: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} used Moses to give these commands and rules to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. He gave them while they were camped on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan River across from Jericho.

decisions.choice: these are the commandments: the close of the laws given on the plains of Moab, and of the book
decisions.reason: Israel camped on the plains of Moab in 22:1, and the laws given there (chiefly chapters 26-36) end with this summary, just as Leviticus ends the laws given at Sinai (Leviticus 27:34). It is also the last verse of Numbers. Moses' farewell speeches in Deuteronomy are given in the same place (Deuteronomy 1:5).

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: The LORD gave the laws, and Moses passed them on to the people. "By the hand of" names the one through whom something is done.

decisions.choice: the Jordan of Jericho: the stretch of the Jordan facing Jericho
decisions.reason: The camp lay on the east side of the river, across from Jericho on the west side (22:1; 33:48-50). Jericho was to be the first city taken in the land (Joshua 6).

decisions.choice: the commandments and the judgments: commands and legal rulings
decisions.reason: The first word names commands to be obeyed, the second rulings for deciding cases, such as the rulings on inheritance in this chapter and in 27:1-11.

decisions.choice: rulings / rules
decisions.reason: Balanced says "rulings" and Readable "rules" for the word Literal gives as "judgments", the wording used for this word throughout Numbers to Ruth.
